blocks.text: they laughed as they remarked, 'This is your commander!' 'O Abu Abdullaah!' I protested, 'Do you not see what they are saying?' 'Leave them alone,' he bade me, 'Good and bad are to be seen after today (in the Aakhirah). If you are able to live off the earth, do so rather than being commander over even two persons. Beware of the curse of the oppressed and those left with no options because there is no barrier to their curses (Allaah accepts it immediately).'"

Another narration states that when Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was the governor of Madaa'in, he would go out to the people wearing his simple lower garment and shawl. When they saw him, the people would say, "Gurg Aamad! Gurg Aamad!" "What are they saying?" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) asked. "They are comparing you to a toy of theirs," the people replied. To this, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) remarked, "It does not matter (what they say). Good will be seen only after this day (in the Aakhirah)."

Hadhrat Huraym reports, "I once saw Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) riding a donkey that was unsaddled. He was wearing a garment made in Sumbulaan which was short for him and was narrow at the bottom. He was a long-legged and hairy man and the garment reached only up to his knees. When I saw some youngsters (mischievously) prodding his donkey on from the back, I rebuked them saying, 'Will you not get away from your Ameer?!' To this, Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said, 'Leave them alone because good and evil will only be seen after this day.'"[^1]

Hadhrat Thaabit reports that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was the governor of Madaa'in when a man arrived from Shaam carrying figs. Because Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) was wearing his simple lower garment and shawl, the man (not recognising Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and thinking him to be a common labourer) called to him saying, "Come and carry this!" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) obliged and when the people saw him and recognised who he was, they exclaimed, "This is the governor!" When the man pleaded that he did not recognise Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) (and wished to take the load back), Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) said to him, "Leave it until I reach your destination."
Another narration states that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) added, "I had already formulated an intention (to please Allaah by this service) and I am therefore unable to put this down until I reach your house."[^2]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Buraydah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) used to make things with his hands and when he earned some money by selling them, he would purchase some meat or fish. He would then invite some lepers to share the meal with him.[^3]
The Humility of Hadhrat Hudhayfah bin Yamaan (RA)
